The package vignettes focus on runnable examples. The technical reference provides a more complete description of the model notation, likelihoods, structured process terms, collapsed sampler, sparse linear algebra, recovery, and prediction machinery used by `stLMM`.

[Download the PDF technical reference](../stLMM-modeling-and-software-details.pdf).

The document is intended for readers who want implementation-level detail beyond the user-facing examples. It is most useful when checking how a model formula maps to the latent process representation, how the collapsed sampler is constructed, or how recovery and prediction use the sampled parameters and retained process draws.

## Innovation representations for separable space-time models

Space-time dependence can also be expressed through spatial innovations, the new latent variation introduced at each time. @OrdonezEtAl2026Innovations use this representation for censored and missing areal tensor data, combining DAGAR spatial dependence with autoregressive temporal dependence and Bayesian computation in Stan.

For example, let $Q_s$ be the marginal spatial precision of a CAR or DAGAR state, including its variance scale. A stationary separable AR(1) model with $|a|<1$ can be written as

$$
w_1\sim N(0,Q_s^{-1}),\qquad
w_t=a w_{t-1}+\eta_t,\qquad
\eta_t\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}N(0,(1-a^2)Q_s^{-1}).
$$

The factor $(1-a^2)$ ensures that every time slice has marginal covariance $Q_s^{-1}$. Stacking the states by time gives the prior precision $Q_t(a)\otimes Q_s$, where $Q_t(a)$ is the inverse AR(1) correlation matrix. Thus the recursive and joint representations describe the same prior under these assumptions. Conditional prior evaluations can operate on spatial innovations rather than factorizing a full space-time matrix. For DAGAR, its triangular parent representation further supplies spatial conditional operations. Irregular time gaps require the corresponding gap-dependent transition and innovation variances.

### Relationship to stLMM's collapsed computation

stLMM integrates structured latent effects out during parameter updates using $M=Q_w+A^\mathsf{T}WA$, where $Q_w$ is their joint prior precision, $A$ maps them to observations, and $W$ is the diagonal observation precision. Augmented non-Gaussian models also draw and retain latent effects within the chain for the augmentation updates, as described in the technical reference. The recursion above specifies the latent prior. An inference engine that samples innovations explicitly would sample a different set of unknowns from stLMM's collapsed parameter updates. A collapsed formulation in terms of innovations would still need to integrate out the latent states while accounting for the observation mappings and any additional process terms.

The current implementation uses a common precision-based calculation across point, areal, temporal, space-time, and varying-coefficient terms. Innovation representations offer a basis for specialized inference with suitable temporal structure, but stLMM does not currently provide an innovation-based inference engine.
